# Ultralyd af tarmen

**Ultralyd af tarmen** (abdominal ultrasound) is an imaging procedure under consideration in some Danish hospital departments as a potential alternative to colonoscopy in the diagnostic workup of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). The procedure appears in quality assurance discussions related to compliance with national IBD diagnostic standards.

According to the DANIBD registry, which monitors diagnostic evaluation of newly diagnosed IBD patients across Danish hospitals and regions, there is variation in how departments conduct their initial investigations. Some departments may substitute colonoscopy with sigmoidoscopy and/or abdominal ultrasound, raising questions about whether these variations reflect resource constraints or deliberate clinical choices [^src1]. The DANIBD registry tracks two key quality indicators: indicator 1a, which monitors colonoscopy evaluation of adults (target 79%, achieved nationally), and indicator 1b, which monitors complete diagnostic workup of children and young people including gastroscopy, colonoscopy, and MR imaging or capsule endoscopy (target 69%) [^src1]. The variation in diagnostic approaches across departments and regions is documented as part of broader efforts to understand compliance gaps and plan future audits scheduled for 2026 [^src1].
